title: Japan 5-Year Climate Transition Bond (GX) auction, issue 6 (¥250bn anticipated, maturity 2031-09-20 derived) — a Dutch-format auction that publishes no tail, three days after the BoJ
source: EST: mof.go.jp English November 2026 auction calendar (english/policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/2611e.htm), re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 25,187 bytes) for this initial research; parsed cell by cell, its first table row reads 'Nov. 2, 2026 | 5-year Japan Climate Transition Bonds', with both the Auction Announcement and Auction Result cells the plain string 'Detail' carrying NO href, and the Non-price-competitive Auction II cell reading '-'. So nothing about this auction has been announced and NO SIZE IS ASSERTED. ¥250bn is the anticipated base case on a FISCAL-YEAR IDENTITY, not a trend extrapolation, and this session established it from MOF's own primaries rather than quoting the proposal: all TWELVE Climate Transition auction announcement pages (announcement/auct{20240207,20240220,20240521,20240711,20241015,20250122,20250708,20251014,20260119,20260306,20260518,20260817}e.htm, all HTTP 200, parsed field by field 2026-09-09) read a single offering amount per Japanese fiscal year — 'About 800 billion yen' for the two inaugural February 2024 auctions, 'About 350 billion yen' for all FOUR of FY2024 (2024-05-28, 2024-07-18, 2024-10-22, 2025-01-29), 'About 300 billion yen' for all FOUR of FY2025 (2025-07-15, 2025-10-21, 2026-01-26, 2026-03-13) and 'About 250 billion yen' for BOTH of FY2026 so far (2026-05-25, 2026-08-24). Eight of eight auctions inside a completed fiscal year carried that year's single constant size. The ANNOUNCEMENT DATE is a measured rule, not the calendar's 'about': the lead is exactly SEVEN calendar days in 12 of 12, putting the 2026-11-02 terms on 2026-10-26, a Monday and a business day (Culture Day falls 11-03, out of the way). THE PROGRAMME RUNS BOTH TENORS AND THE PROPOSAL SAW ONLY ONE: MOF's calendars 2401e-2610e (34 files, all HTTP 200; 2612e 404s) carry twelve Climate Transition rows alternating 10-year and 5-year, four per fiscal year since FY2024 — which is what makes the size a fiscal-year constant rather than the 'monotone decline' a 5-year-only reading produces. Filed `estimate` on this lane's no-self-confirm limit, because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office, and because the size is anticipated rather than announced. The DATE is MOF's own and is not in doubt. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Canonical file written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, from the single sibling proposal `proposals/jgb-climate-transition-5y-auction-2026-11-02.from-jgb-5y-auction-2026-11-12.json` (now shadowed and left in place). THE PROPOSAL'S STATED JOB IS REFUTED BY THE AUCTION'S OWN FORMAT. It proposed this entry to give the 5-year sector 'a second, differently-structured demand read' via cover and tail. All twelve GX announcement pages carry the note '* The auction method is Dutch-style-yield-competitive auction at intervals of 0.1bp' — a note the regular 5-year's announcement (auct20260511e.htm, HTTP 200) does NOT carry — and all twelve GX result pages print '-' for both Weighted Average Price and Yield at the Average Price. A uniform-price auction has ONE clearing yield, so a tail (highest accepted minus average) is IDENTICALLY ZERO BY CONSTRUCTION: the entire ≥2bp / per-tenor-p90 tail apparatus four sibling ledgers built is UNDEFINED here, not merely unpublished. AND THE COVER RATIO IS A SIZE ARTIFACT: across the ten non-inaugural GX auctions, yen bid volume is near-constant at ¥1,115.3bn (sd ¥137.5, cv 12.3%) while the offering fell ¥350bn → ¥250bn (−28.6%), so corr(offer size, cover) = −0.478 (10-year −0.877). At the 5-year specifically, cover rose 3.192 → 4.622 (+44.8%) from 2025-01-29 to 2026-05-25 while bids rose ¥1,116.4 → ¥1,155.6bn (+3.5%). The artifact was caught in the act on 2026-08-24, when the 10-year GX drew ¥875.9bn — the LOWEST bid volume of the whole programme — and covered 3.505, its second best. THE ONE HONEST READ IS YEN BID VOLUME. WHAT THE ENTRY IS ACTUALLY WORTH: (1) it is the FIRST Japanese coupon auction after the 2026-10-30 BoJ decision — October's last is the 2-year on Oct 29 (2610e.htm) and MOF's next calendar row is this one — so the tape's first read on the BoJ lands on the auction least able to say anything; (2) it is a same-maturity twin of the regular 5-year, 5 of 5 — every GX 5-year issue carries exactly the maturity of the regular 5-year auctioned earlier in the same quarter (2028-12-20/165, 2029-06-20/170, 2030-06-20/179, 2030-12-20/183, 2031-03-20/185, all read off MOF result pages), which puts issue 6 at maturity 2031-09-20 and agrees with the sibling ledger's independent derivation; (3) matched on that maturity and netted against MOF's own par curve on each auction's own date, THERE IS NO GREENIUM — mean −0.64bp, median +0.18bp, sd 3.30bp, t = −0.43, n=5. Scale: ¥250bn is 12.9% of the regular 5-year's COMPETITIVE tranche (~¥1,932bn of its ¥2,500bn headline; the GX has no non-competitive tranche at all) and 39.0% of one month's entire BoJ 3-5y absorption (¥641.0bn in 2026-08, re-derived this session from ope2608.xlsx rather than quoted). NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is low for the reason every sibling JGB ledger records: no tracked symbol carries yen-rates exposure and no house playbook is rates-keyed. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
